conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds. Both classify pMCI against sMCI in ADNI MCI from structural MRI. Horizon (P-182: follow-up at least 18 months; P-122: progression within three years), input, architecture and unit of analysis differ, which condition 1 allows.
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Holds. Accuracy with accuracy, AUC with AUC.
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds. Neither paper reports a result under the other's condition: P-122 has no single-timepoint, hippocampal-box, AD/CN-transfer or subject-level figure, and P-182 has no two-timepoint figure. The ablation the reader leans on (unimproved Eff-GCNet, 71.6%, AUC 0.7770) removes P-122's own modules while keeping P-122's two-timepoint whole-brain input, its three-year label, its MCI-trained target and its sample-level test. None of P-182's conditions is applied, and P-182's model is a two-stream 3D DenseNet, not Eff-GCNet. So it is not a matched figure. Nor does it show that the architecture difference between these two papers accounts for their gap. It shows that P-122's modules are worth 11 to 13 points on P-122's own input. For that to account for the cross-paper gap, the other differences (input, region, training target, label window) would have to net out against P-122 by about 4 points (71.6 vs 75.85), and neither paper tests that. P-182 itself names the missing longitudinal imaging and the single modality as things that may have lowered its performance. The ablation is also weaker evidence than the reading credits. (a) Every ablation and backbone row in Tables 3-4 is consistent with whole-number counts only for a test set of 42 positive and 60 negative cases (or multiples), not the stated 124-sample test. Example: 71.6% = (34 + 39)/102. (b) On that set the full model's own sensitivity (83.33%) and specificity (82.27%) imply 82.7%. The 84.74% headline exceeds both its sensitivity and its specificity, which no single confusion matrix can do. This fits the paper's statement that its final metrics were aggregated across the two validation schemes. (c) At about 34 test subjects (102 x 275/823), the ablated 71.6% has a Wilson interval of 0.549-0.839, which contains the full model's 0.827. So at subject level the module effect itself is not beyond uncertainty. At sample level (n = 102, 0.622-0.794) it is. Finally, if a within-paper ablation that lands near the other paper's figure counted as showing sufficiency, nearly every method-versus-method pair would fail: ablated baselines routinely land at prior published levels. P-122's own Table 5 lists 13 prior pMCI/sMCI results at 71.07-83.51%. That is the outcome the operator's direction rules out.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds in both directions. P-182 accuracy Wilson (n = 381): 0.713-0.799. It excludes P-122's CV 0.8428, its test 0.8474 and the implied 0.827. P-122 CV accuracy Wilson (n = 275 subjects): 0.795-0.881, which excludes 0.7585. AUC: P-182 Hanley-McNeil (118/263) 0.723-0.831 excludes 0.8599. P-122 CV Hanley-McNeil (121/154) 0.814-0.906 excludes 0.777. Two-sample checks: accuracy z = 2.72, AUC z = 2.28.
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds: 0.8474/0.8587 and 0.7585/0.777 are below 0.97. P-182's 94.07%/0.993 is one AD-vs-CN training fold, not a compared figure.
conditions_attacked.6_record: Holds. The compared figures are the ones the papers print. The registry modality 'MRI/PET' is wrong but does not create the gap. P-122's headline is internally inconsistent (see 3b), but its CV figure (84.28%) and its implied single-split figure (82.7%) both still lie outside P-182's interval.

figures.P-122: Six-fold CV over 275 subjects (823 samples): Acc 0.8428, Wilson 0.795-0.881. AUC 0.8599, Hanley-McNeil (121/154) SE 0.0236, CI 0.814-0.906. The headline 84.74%/0.8587 is aggregated; the single split implied by its sensitivity/specificity is about 82.7% (Wilson on 102 cases 0.742-0.888). Ablation (unimproved Eff-GCNet): 71.6%, AUC 0.7770. Wilson 0.622-0.794 on 102 cases, 0.549-0.839 on about 34 subjects.

results.not_shown_sufficient: No candidate explanation is shown sufficient for the cross-paper gap. P-122's ablation shows the size of its own module effect on its own input only, and that effect is not beyond uncertainty at subject level.
results.reason: No figure in either paper is under the other's condition. P-122's architecture ablation keeps P-122's two-timepoint input, label and target, so it neither matches P-182's condition nor shows that architecture accounts for the cross-paper gap. The ablation's own test set does not match the stated one, and its effect is within subject-level uncertainty. Every other condition holds, with the gap beyond uncertainty in both directions (accuracy z = 2.72, AUC z = 2.28). This verdict rests on the reading that a paper's ablation of its own modules is a candidate explanation, not a condition-3 failure. If the operator rules otherwise, C-117 and C-147 both fail condition 3, and the ruling must then be applied to every method-versus-method pair.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds. Both predict three-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI from baseline T1 sMRI. P-207 MCI-c converted within 3-year follow-up; P-185 separates pMCI/sMCI at 3 years. The ledger's EEG/MEG modality for P-207 is wrong. Features within the channel differ, which condition 1 allows.
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Holds. Accuracy with accuracy (P-207's MCI-c vs MCI-nc 87.72%, not the ledger's 90.44% AD-vs-NC figure).
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds. Neither paper evaluates the other's features, classifier or subjects. The agreeing baselines are each paper's own condition, not the other's. P-207's OFMROI (64.15%) is VBM grey-matter volume of the top three AAL ROIs within ICA network templates, fed to AdaBoost with linear-SVM learners. P-185's original morphological features (62.92%) are FreeSurfer cortical thickness and volume with mRMR plus SVM-RFE and an RBF SVM, the protocol of its reference [13]. That the two agree is the reader's cross-paper inference; neither paper shows it. Chaining the two ablations says only that each paper's figure departs from a plain baseline in its own representation. That restates the discrepancy (two feature-extraction methods for the same question give 87.7% and 69.4%) rather than dissolving it, and features within the channel are an allowed difference to be recorded as a candidate explanation. On the 'best of 15' point: P-207 gives E1 = 3, E2 = 2 as the setting that was best for AD vs NC, and says the same selection applies to MCI. So 87.72% is P-207's recommended setting, carried over from the AD/NC task, not only the maximum of the MCI grid. Whether the setting was fixed before the MCI runs is not stated. Even the median of the 15 CFMnetwork settings (75.71%; mean 76.24%) lies above P-185's upper bound of 0.751. Only the lowest settings (70.24%, 70.65%) fall inside it. Parameter sensitivity is a candidate explanation, not a figure under P-185's condition, and P-185 also tuned every method's parameters.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds in both directions. P-207 Wilson (n = 234): 0.829-0.913. P-185 Wilson (n = 221): 0.630-0.751. Two-sample z = 4.87.
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds: 87.72% and 69.37% are below 0.97, as is P-207's highest figure (90.44%, AD vs NC).
conditions_attacked.6_record: Holds. The ledger's 90.44% is a misread (AD vs NC), but the printed conversion figure (87.72%) still differs beyond uncertainty, so the misread does not create the gap. The record must quote 87.72% and sMRI.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds once the right document is read: P-186 vs Bae et al. (P-37), 36-month MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, with MRI as the shared channel. The P-174 PDF is a MEG paper and prints no 0.827.
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Fails, though the case for passing is real. The case for passing: the ledger's 0.957 comes from P-186's one-year-ahead experiment on 85 subjects. The figure that changes only the channel to Bae's is the one-year MRI-only AUC, 0.905, on the same 85 subjects. Its Hanley-McNeil interval (35/50) is 0.833-0.977, which excludes Bae's 0.827 by 0.006. The bound still excludes 0.827 with the class roles swapped (0.841-0.969), and the rule has no tolerance term. Why it fails anyway: P-186 reports its MRI-only result under two forecasting settings. Both use the same 36-month label, the same contrast and the same MRI-only channel, and neither uses Bae's single-timepoint input, so the two are equally matched to Bae's condition. The six-month-ahead MRI-only figure (0.88, n = 119, CI 0.813-0.947) agrees with Bae's 0.827 (0.729-0.925) in both directions. The one-year figure misses by an approximation-sized margin (two-sample z = 1.26). That estimate is also a fold-averaged AUC whose markers were ranked on the full normalised dataset (Figure 1: 'Full Normalized Longitudinal Dataset (n=85)' feeds 'Marker Ranking' before the CV split), with the marker count chosen as the best on the evaluation folds. That optimism, if removed, would move P-186 toward Bae. The papers' own channel-matched data therefore reconcile the pair at one setting and leave only an approximation-sized residual at the other. If the operator treats the one-year experiment as the only counterpart of the recorded figure and applies the bound strictly, the pair qualifies by 0.006; I do not recommend that reading.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Headline figures are separated (0.908-1.000 vs 0.729-0.925). Channel-matched: one year, one direction by 0.006; six months, no separation.
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds on the compared figures (0.957, 0.905, 0.88, 0.827 are all below 0.97). P-186's ground-truth 0.98 uses observed future values and is not compared.
conditions_attacked.6_record: The ledger pair must be repointed from P-174 to P-37.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds: three-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, with MRI as the shared channel. P-211 uses baseline FreeSurfer regional measures in an EBM; Bae et al. (P-37, the document behind the ledger's P-174 figure) use a 3D CNN on the baseline T1.
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds. The reader's matched figure missed P-211's primary three-year results. The 0.81 is a side analysis of Comb (a) with and without interactions 'in the test dataset', the 10% hold-out (about 58 people). Comb (a) also adds cognitive scores (ADAS13, MMSE, FAQ, CDR-SB) to MRI. P-211's primary results are the 5-fold CV means in Figure 2(d), which the text does not print as numbers. I measured them from the PDF rendered at 8x: the axis runs from 0 at y = 1304 px to 1.0 at y = 394.5 px. At three years, Comb (c) (green triangle) sits at 0.704, SD bar 0.693-0.714. Comb (a) (red) is 0.754 and Comb (b) is 0.752. Read-off precision is about +/-0.01, and the C-151 reader independently read the same values. Comb (c) is 'MRI-driven biomarkers, plus age, gender, education, diagnose at baseline, and APOE4', from baseline input, at the three-year horizon. It matches Bae on horizon, single-timepoint input, contrast and channel, so it is the best-matched figure in either paper. Hanley-McNeil over the CV portion of the three-year set (about 169 dementia/353 MCI) gives SE 0.0254 and CI 0.654-0.754, which excludes Bae's 0.827. Bae's CI (0.729-0.925) excludes 0.704. Two-sample z = 2.20. The best-matched figure therefore does not reconcile the pair; the gap persists, reversed. Comb (a)'s CV three-year figure (0.754, CI 0.707-0.801) also excludes 0.827 in one direction. Only the small, less-matched side-analysis figure (0.81, CI 0.681-0.939) agrees. Comb (c)'s extra non-MRI inputs (age, baseline EMCI/LMCI, APOE4) would be expected to raise P-211's AUC, so the reverse gap is conservative. P-211's text agrees: performance dips at two to three years, and it recommends cognitive measures for mid-term prediction.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds in both directions on the best-matched figures (0.704 outside 0.729-0.925; 0.827 outside 0.654-0.754). This holds whether the CV n is taken as 169/353 or the full 188/392 (CI 0.657-0.751).

cross_cutting: C-117 and C-147 turn on one ruling: whether a paper's ablation of its own modules or features, whose baseline lands near the other paper's figure, counts as a condition-3 failure. This file reads it as a candidate explanation, because condition 3 names the other paper's condition and condition 1 allows architecture and feature differences. Whichever way the operator rules, the ruling should be applied to every method-versus-method pair.

C-149's reversal uses the same Figure 2(d) reading the C-151 reader made. C-150's reader, like C-149's, reportedly used only the 0.81, so C-150 should be rechecked against Comb (c) at the matched horizon.

P-122's headline (84.74% with sensitivity 83.33% and specificity 82.27%) is arithmetically impossible for a single confusion matrix, and its ablation tables fit a 102-case test, not the stated 124. Anywhere P-122's headline is cited, it should be treated as an aggregate.
